finding: We tested whether an imperfect cue about the source prior improves storage choices. With a cue that is correct two-thirds of the time, accounting for its errors improves retained coverage in 147 of 420 distinct problems. Treating the cue as certain performs worse than ignoring it in 276. Independent rational reconstruction and both full replays verify this constructed-method result; it does not establish forecast accuracy or process correspondence.
